s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disease with autoimmune features, characterized by skin, joint, and lung involvement, with a prolonged time course and significant weight loss
salient_findings: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints
Dorsal ulcers and dyspigmentation of distal fingers
Bibasilar rales and interstitial lung disease on chest CT
Elevated ferritin and lymphocytopenia
Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies
key_facts: 7-month history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, and hand swelling
50-pound weight loss
Previous hospitalization for hypoxia
Prior treatment with prednisone
Normal capillaroscopy
Ulcerated lichenoid papules on palmar IP creases
Oxford Scale muscle strength 5 of 5 throughout
Depressed creatine kinase
Elevated ferritin
Lymphocytopenia with CD3, CD4, and CD8 counts provided
Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies
Positive immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies
Negative results for HIV, anti-Scl-70 antibodies, and lupus anticoagulant
Normal prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time
Chest CT showing hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities
Worsening interstitial lung disease on follow-up Chest CT
Bronchoscopy revealing plaquelike lesions
Transbronchial nodal aspiration of mediastinal nodes negative for carcinomas/granulomas
Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity
Skin biopsy showing orthokeratosis, rare lymphocytes at dermal/epidermal junction, and diffuse vasculopathy
